endpoints.analysis_population: Modified Intent-to-Treat (MITT) Population, defined as all subjects who are injected with study drug, have a valid Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) score at Baseline (Day 1) visit and at least one valid MAS score and valid Clinical Global Impression of Change (CGI-C) score at the Week 4 post-baseline visit in the Double-Blind Phase of the study.
endpoints.description:
The Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) is an internationally accepted and validated instrument used to measure resistance during passive soft-tissue stretching.
Resistance will be measured and recorded using a 6-point scale ranging from 0 (no increase in muscle tone) to 4 (affected part[s] rigid in flexion or extension).
The post-injection MAS score is subtracted from the baseline MAS score to yield the change from baseline MAS score.
A change from baseline MAS score <0 represents a better outcome.
endpoints.measure: The Change From Baseline in Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) Score for Tone of the Primary Target Muscle Group (PTMG) Selected for Treatment at Week 4 Post-injection.

你是一名临床试验终点预测与循证医学分析专家。

你的任务是：基于知识截止日期之前公开可获得的证据，预测临床试验指定终点的结果。

规则：
1. 这是预测任务，不是结果检索任务。
2. 即使直接证据不足，也必须尽力给出预测。
3. 证据不足时，应降低 confidence，并明确说明不确定性，但不能仅因为证据不足而拒绝预测。
4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。
6. 不得把试验状态、论文发表、药物批准或模型评分直接视为终点成功证据。
7. 每个 endpoint_id 必须单独预测。
8. 每个治疗组、时间点和统计目标必须单独保留。
9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。
10. 但必须输出完整、可公开审计的证据分析，包括证据来源、证据类型、证据与预测之间的联系以及主要不确定性。
11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。
13. 证据来源必须可追溯：只有当前会话工具成功返回的公开记录、正文片段和 URL 才能称为“已检索证据”。工具返回 returned=0、source_unavailable 或空 results 时，不得把该来源当作证据。
14. 如果提到模型既有知识中的外部试验或论文，但当前会话没有成功检索并冻结其内容，必须明确标注为“未核验背景先验/假设”，不得写入 search_verification，也不得伪装成已查到的引用。
15. 当注册库和文献检索均失败或均无结果时，仍需完成可映射终点的预测，但必须显著降低 confidence（通常不高于 0.30），明确说明证据缺口；不得把试验设计、分组、样本量写成检索所得事实，只能使用动态装载的试验上下文。
16. 每条外部资料在使用前必须核对人群、药物/剂量、适应证、endpoint定义、测量单位、时间点、对照组和estimand。完全匹配的资料才可支持精确数值；同药物或相近人群资料通常只能支持方向或范围。

analysis_trace.finding: NCT04815967: Phase 3 efficacy/safety study of MYOBLOC (rimabotulinumtoxinB, botulinum toxin type B) vs placebo in adult upper limb spasticity. Two-stage design: Phase 2 dose-finding (10,000U vs 20,000U vs placebo) then Phase 3 (MYOBLOC vs placebo). Primary timepoint one year; secondary endpoints at ~13-week intervals over ≥1 year.

Adult upper limb spasticity (post-stroke/traumatic brain injury upper motor neuron syndrome). MYOBLOC is FDA-approved for cervical dystonia and sialorrhea, not yet for spasticity; this trial seeks a new indication.

Adults with upper limb spasticity. Registry record unavailable (HTTP 403), so exact inclusion criteria (etiology, Modified Ashworth Scale threshold, prior toxin exposure) are unknown. Companion lower-limb study NCT04099667 exists, suggesting a parallel spasticity program.

RimabotulinumtoxinB (serotype B) cleaves VAMP/synaptobrevin, blocking acetylcholine release at neuromuscular junction, reducing muscle overactivity. Mechanism is well-established and shared with botulinum toxin A products proven effective in upper limb spasticity.

Primary endpoint is efficacy vs placebo (likely Modified Ashworth Scale or muscle tone reduction) at one year. Secondary-1 is dose response (10k vs 20k vs placebo); secondary-2 is duration of response after single administration; secondary-3/4 are long-term safety/tolerability after multiple administrations.

Botulinum toxin B has known adverse events: dry mouth, dysphagia, injection-site reactions, and higher immunogenicity/antibody formation than type A (secondary treatment failure risk). Long-term safety profile is established in cervical dystonia and sialorrhea populations.

Higher immunogenicity of type B vs type A may limit long-term efficacy; dose-dependent autonomic side effects (dry mouth, dysphagia) at 10,000-20,000U; no prior spasticity approval for this serotype; unknown whether efficacy in spasticity matches cervical dystonia.

No direct numeric result for this trial is available pre-cutoff. Indirect evidence: botulinum toxin A products (onabotulinumtoxinA, incobotulinumtoxinA, abobotulinumtoxinA) consistently show significant efficacy in upper limb spasticity; MYOBLOC is effective in cervical dystonia (Cochrane review) and sialorrhea. Mechanism is shared, supporting a positive efficacy forecast, but type B's higher immunogenicity and lack of spasticity-specific data widen uncertainty.

Registry record (NCT04815967) returned HTTP 403; crossref/europepmc records are living records not fetchable at cutoff. No direct trial results, no spasticity-specific MYOBLOC efficacy data, no exact endpoint definitions (MAS scale, responder threshold) retrievable. All numeric forecasts are extrapolations from related indications.
